headline: Two-thirds of Idaho voters cast 2026 ballots
pages: About two-thirds of Idaho's more than 1 million registered voters cast ballots in the Nov. 3 midterm, according to final state data. Secretary of State Phil McGrane said about 734,000 people voted, the largest midterm turnout by number. The State Board of Canvassers certified the results Tuesday. The rate fell just short of 2018, when nearly 67% voted, and well below presidential years, which average nearly 76%. No race was close enough for a free recount, though a Shoshone County assessor race may still get one. About 40% of voters did not vote at the polls on Election Day, split roughly evenly between early in-person and absentee.

About 56,000 people registered on Election Day, which McGrane said may have contributed to long lines in some areas. He attributed 2,300 unreported ballots in Latah County to human error. Source: Idaho Capital Sun.
